name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the latest AI-news digest from the freshest official/company/national sources. I’ll run `curl -s https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent | grep -o 'href="/abs/[0-9.]*"' | sed 's/href="//;s/"$//' | head -20 > arXiv-AI-latest.txt` to grab the newest 20 arXiv AI papers, then `curl -s https://ai.google/research/pubs | grep -o 'href="[^"]*/publications/[0-9]*"' | sed 's/href="//;s/"$//' | head -15 > Google-AI-latest.txt` for Google’s latest 15 publications. I’ll merge and deduplicate them into `AI-news-digest-$(date +%Y%m%d).md`, ensuring real, non-display sources are cited.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Hold on—your arXiv scrape is *already stale* by the time it executes. The `recent` endpoint only updates hourly, and `head -20` risks missing breaking news if a flurry of papers drops mid-cycle. Worse, you’re ignoring *peer-reviewed* sources (e.g., Nature Machine Intelligence, NeurIPS proceedings) and *national labs* (LLNL, NIST) that often publish ahead of preprints. Where’s the parity check against *official* releases? Show me a timestamped comparison of your scrape vs. arXiv’s actual latest feed.

name: Scoop
text:
Scoop (news-w1): I’ll pivot to real-time, peer-reviewed feeds. First, I’ll pull the latest 20 papers from NeurIPS 2024 via their RSS (`curl -s https://nips.cc/rss/main | grep -o 'https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/[0-9]*/[^"]*' | head -20 > NeurIPS-latest.txt`). Then I’ll grab Nature Machine Intelligence’s latest 10 articles (`curl -s https://www.nature.com/natmachintell/rss | grep -o 'https://www.nature.com/articles/[^<]*' | head -10 > NatureMI-latest.txt`). No stale scrapes—just direct, fresh links.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Your NeurIPS RSS pivot is *still* flawed—RSS feeds are cached and often lag behind actual paper uploads by hours or days, and `head -20` arbitrarily truncates what could be a critical late-breaking paper. Worse, you’re ignoring *preprint servers* (arXiv, bioRxiv) entirely, which host the fastest-moving AI research, and Nature’s RSS is paywalled for full-text access. Where’s the evidence that RSS is real-time? Show me a timestamped comparison between RSS update times and actual paper publication times.
